items.text: Buy-side coverage
Private equity and platform acquirers
The clock is running and the exit door is narrower.
A sponsor can leave an end market that a permanent holder cannot. That advantage is worth less than it was. Holds are longer, software exits are down, and the return has moved into the add-ons.

For buyers · The holding period
years: the technology holding period at exit in 2026 to date. In 2021 it was 4.5 years.

PrivateEquityInfo, 7 September 2026: 13,757 exits across nine industries, 2,586 of them in technology. The study folds software into technology; no named publisher reports a software-only figure for 2026.

items.text: For buyers · Where the return now sits
Six and a half times in, nine times out. The end market decides whether that spread survives to exit.

The step-up between an add-on multiple and a platform multiple is what the market pays for scale in one end market, on the day you sell. The exit buyer will run the end-market work on your customer base.
What private equity paid for add-ons at $2M to $5M of EBITDA
Against 7.6 times at enterprise values of $25M to $50M, and 9.4 times at $50M to $200M.
Add-ons’ approximate share of US software private equity deal value
More than doubled. Platform buyouts fell to 41 percent of deal value, the lowest in at least a decade.
Software sponsor exits by value, first half of 2026
Roughly $32bn on 111 deals. The number of deals was down 22 percent on the year.
Broken letters of intent that died on a finding outside the earnings work
Up from 19.1 percent in 2023, while financing fell from 21.3 to 10.7 percent. What ends deals has moved from the balance sheet to the business.

TagniFi PowerComps, Q2 2026; the multiples are the provider’s own figures, published in a piece written by its managing director. PitchBook, 25 June 2026. ION Analytics / Mergermarket, 15 July 2026. A lower-middle-market deal platform’s published study of broken letters of intent, 27 January 2026: seventy-five broken letters across eight buyer types and eight industries, with 2023 comparisons from the same series. The percentages are separate reported categories and are not summed here. That study covers all industries and does not break its diligence category down further.
